=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: 1696-1700 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: When a CI workflow run on the default branch is classified as `workflow-defect` or `inconclusive` (UPSTREAM_ISSUE_CLASSIFICATIONS), `compose_issue_body` checks only `payload.get("source_kind") == "workflow_run"` and emits the intro text "A release / promotion workflow run failed." This is misleading for CI-on-main failures, which are not release/promotion runs. The same check at line 1631 for non-UPSTREAM_ISSUE_CLASSIFICATIONS has the same blind spot.
  WHY: A heal issue filed for a red `main` CI failure will state "A release / promotion workflow run failed" in its body, confusing operators who read the issue and may look in the wrong place (release logs instead of CI logs).
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: 68 (MAIN_CI_WORKFLOW_NAMES constant definition) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `MAIN_CI_WORKFLOW_NAMES` is defined but never consumed by any logic in `workflow_failure_heal.py` or `workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh`. It is referenced only by `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py` (line 138-139). The constant has no effect on classification, body composition, or routing — the intake's `if:` condition in the workflow YAML is the sole gate for CI events. This is dead code at runtime that looks like active routing.
  WHY: An operator reading the code would expect `MAIN_CI_WORKFLOW_NAMES` to influence body composition or target-branch selection, but it does neither. The intake's YAML-level `if:` guard is the only filter. If a future `workflow_run` event with a different name (not "CI") were added to the intake, the constant would have no effect and the intake would silently route it as a release workflow.
- workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml: lines 17-18 (workflow_run: workflows: ["*"]) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The consumer wrapper listens to every workflow with `workflows: ["*"]`. Every completed workflow run in the consumer — including every `AI Review`, `AI Implement`, `AI Clarify`, etc. — dispatches the triage wrapper, which then evaluates the `triage-workflow-run` job condition and skips itself (because the name starts with `AI `). This creates one skipped wrapper run per consumer workflow run.
  WHY: Each wrapper run appears in the Actions tab and consumes a workflow-dispatch event, increasing UI noise linearly with overall workflow activity. While the PR description documents this trade-off ("each finished workflow also leaves a skipped wrapper run in the Actions tab"), it bears repeating as a deliberate but noisy side effect with no functional failure.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "MAIN_CI_WORKFLOW_NAMES in scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py" — the PR description states this constant should inform the heal intake's routing/target for CI-on-main failures, specifically "the heal issue targets the failed run's branch (`main`), through the existing `failed_run_branch` routing."
  Expected change site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py `compose_issue_body()` — around line 1631 or 1696, and/or `target_branch_for_issue()` — to check whether the workflow name is in MAIN_CI_WORKFLOW_NAMES and adjust the body text and/or target branch accordingly.
  Evidence of absence: No code in `workflow_failure_heal.py` or `workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh` reads `MAIN_CI_WORKFLOW_NAMES` to influence routing, body text, or target branch selection. The constant is defined at line 68 but is consumed only by the test at `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:138-139`. The PR diff's `compose_issue_body` text at line 1696-1700 unconditionally says "A release / promotion workflow run failed" for all `workflow_run` source kinds (including CI). The PR description says "the heal issue targets `main`, the failed run's branch" — the intake already deduces the target branch from the workflow payload, so the constant may not need to change routing, but the body text should distinguish CI from release workflows.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml: Line 18 (workflows: ["*"]) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: GitHub Actions does not support wildcard patterns in on.workflow_run.workflows.
  WHY: GitHub Actions workflow_run syntax requires an exact array of workflow names or file paths, not wildcards. Specifying ["*"] causes GitHub Actions to search for an upstream workflow literally named "*". As a result, the triage-workflow-run job will never trigger for any CI workflow run in consumer repositories, leaving consumer CI failure triage completely inoperative.
- tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py: Lines 104-114 (test_consumer_wrapper_listens_to_every_workflow_but_its_own) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test verifies workflows: ["*"] against a custom _evaluate mock function that assumes wildcard matching is supported for arbitrary workflow names such as "Tests".
  WHY: The test passes against the Python evaluator mock while masking the fact that GitHub Actions itself does not support wildcards in on.workflow_run.workflows and will never dispatch the event in consumer repositories.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py: Lines 1696-1700 (compose_issue_body) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: compose_issue_body unconditionally states that a release or promotion workflow run failed whenever source_kind is workflow_run.
  WHY: When CI fails on main, payload["source_kind"] is workflow_run and payload["workflow_name"] is "CI". The generated issue body text claims "A release / promotion workflow run failed", which injects incorrect failure context into the automated cla
